page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. It features 40 physical cores and 40 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz with a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.8 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this server in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is measured at 1438.99, while multi-core performance reaches 38378.07. In memory operations, it achieves a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations via Passmark score at 14249.04, and Redis SET operations reach 34.78 million operations per second. For lightweight language model tasks, the instance processes 1841.39 tokens per second for prompts using a 135M model, but drops to 56.94 tokens per second for a 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical core allocation offers predictable compute performance without hyperthreading overhead, making it suitable for workloads requiring consistent CPU execution. However, the lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which may introduce latency and additional configuration complexity. The 12 Gbps network baseline is moderate for a 40-core instance, presenting a potential bottleneck for highly distributed data-transfer tasks.

This instance is suited for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from high single-thread performance and dedicated CPU resources, such as software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. It is also applicable for static web serving and moderate-scale text or image processing tasks.
